# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 16:56 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 199 active entries of tips_notebook.json (26 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

A Tracker's public death by Katana on the night after it claims a visit, combined with a Medic protecting someone else, is a strong clue the Medic claim is false; check whether protections were on the Katana victim before voting the Medic.

tips_feedback.tip: Post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current.
tips_feedback.why: Posting my Tracker result early let Bob's visit corroboration carry weight, and Dave's will recorded the lead even after death.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction.
tips_feedback.why: The missing Sheriff visit on Alice's Lookout list was a concrete contradiction that justified the Grace hanging and kept the vote grounded.

tips_feedback.tip: A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Alice and Bob were repeatedly targeted and died, which pointed Village toward them as genuine roles even though the Yakuza used that pattern against us.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's census trios were used as slot math to isolate Frank as the only name in every trio, which drove the final nomination debate.

lessons.applies_to: Wiretap or any role that reads private messages
lessons.tip: Use a passive reader silently. Quoting a private message word for word proves you read it, and a Good player who was a recipient will test that. If you must explain a leak, keep the claim vague and avoid verbatim quotes.

Once Yakuza are level with Good (for example two Yakuza against two Good), a trial that hangs a Good player wins the game. Count the endgame arithmetic before each nomination, and don't spend a rig or a vote on a Day that doesn't end the game.
Keep the Clerk rig for the Day when a Good nominee is certain and the rig ends the game. Holding the last token past the point where it could have forced the final hanging wasted the win.

A Jester nominated by the village is a known revenge risk. If you vote Guilty as a group, one of your own Guilty voters can be killed by the revenge. Vote Innocent or abstain from the Guilty bloc on a probable Jester.
Kill the player who is building a visit or census picture, like a Lookout or Census Taker, when the Good side is splitting between claims. That removes the only evidence that could clear a teammate.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester.
tips_feedback.why: We voted Guilty as a group on Grace, a Jester. Her revenge then killed Ivan, a Yakuza who had voted Guilty, so the team lost a member for nothing.

tips_feedback.tip: No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them.
tips_feedback.why: Avoiding PMs between Yakuza kept the team's coordination out of reach, although Erin and Judy did still exchange a PM on Day 5.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim safely: never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's Eavesdropper claim was tied to a PM quote that only two players could have read, so Carol and Heidi could challenge it and it drew the trial.

lessons.tip: Build a written census/visit ledger each day: list every trio or group with its result and check which single player appears in all of them; the odd player out between trios is the best lead.

Avoid a 'hang the Good nominee for a Yakuza win' argument as Village: the Yakuza nominated and hanged the only Good voter, so a Vanilla who pushed for hangings should be checked against its own voting record, not its claim.
Do not pile on a thin nominee early: Grace was a Jester hanged on a single Sheriff claim, and the Village's 10-0 hang handed the Jester a win while Yakuza lost their nightly kill rhythm.

Kill the Lookout and Census Taker before the Medic when the Medic is the only protector; the Katana attacked Dave with a Medic protecting Carol, so protection targeting should be checked against the likely Katana victim.
When a private message's contents are quoted publicly, treat it as a possible Wiretap/Eavesdropper read and ask the quoter to prove access before voting on the PM alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Vote on contradictions, not on who pushed hardest; a claim without a concrete contradiction is not a reason to hang.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Frank both argued from consistent visit lists, and I kept my vote on checkable facts rather than on push intensity, which let me see Frank's census-trio pattern clearly.

tips_feedback.tip: Never say you saved anyone; keep wills current and post results publicly by day.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi and Alice kept clear public result trails, which made their contradictions easy to test against the census and visit lists.

tips_feedback.tip: Check a claim against the visit evidence before voting.
tips_feedback.why: Alice's Lookout list exposing the missing Sheriff visit was the decisive contradiction on Grace, and that vote was well grounded.

lessons.tip: A Jester's win needs a hanging, so it helps to get nominated early with a claim that visibly conflicts with a public lookout list; players who accept a visible contradiction vote quickly. This worked, but it was also a cheap win the Village could see coming.

Census trios that overlap cannot be solved on their own; when one name sits in every trio, the census-taker's own claimed Good result is the only thing that can be checked, so don't let a single overlap decide a hanging.

Before a nomination, the Yakuza should agree on which Village player is the real threat; rotating the Katana holder after each attack would have made the holder harder to pin down by Lookouts and Trackers.

Private messages between two Village players can be read by an Eavesdropper or Wiretap, so any quoted private message that only two people could see is a strong lead; a Yakuza should avoid private messages during the Day entirely.
Vote counts are secret in this variant, so a public claim that a player 'voted Guilty' is unverifiable; weigh public statements and the total counts, not individual vote claims.

tips_feedback.tip: Vote Innocent on a claim that is contradicted by a corroborated result, and explain the contradiction before the vote.
tips_feedback.why: Alice's Lookout list gave a concrete missing visit that players could check, and the Village used it to hang me as the Jester.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza kept their target discussion inside the night chat, so the Village never learned who would be attacked.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads.
tips_feedback.why: Players who stated a clear read and then voted it were easier to evaluate, and the Village converged on those with contradictions.

lessons.tip: Ignite as soon as you are suspected or once two or more living players are doused. Dousing alone gains nothing if you are hanged first, and doused players who die before the ignition are lost value. I reached Day 3 with doused players and no ignition, then was hanged.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza and Neutral players who fake a claim
lessons.tip: A fake claim's protections and results must fit the public night outcomes. My Medic claim protected Carol while Dave died unprotected, which exposed the lie. Choose a cover story that explains the actual deaths.
When someone quotes a private message, ask which role lets them read it before any vote. Only a few roles can read private chats, so the answer narrows the suspect pool quickly.

Do not let a single unverified claim produce a unanimous first-Day hanging. Grace was hanged 10-0 on one Sheriff claim and was the Jester, so ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged before the trial.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: I followed the wait-for-3-doused plan, never ignited, and was hanged on Day 3 with no kills, which is exactly the failure the tip warns about.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar.
tips_feedback.why: Checking the timing of Carol's profile claim against the Night 2 result showed a real problem in my own Medic story, and it sharpened which contradictions were worth voting on.

lessons.tip: A Jester's revenge hits a random living Guilty voter from their trial, so a unanimous Guilty vote on a suspected Jester can kill one of your own. When a Jester is possible, vote Innocent or split the Guilty votes, and avoid having the Katana holder be a Guilty voter.

Plan the Katana holder so that a holder's death from revenge or the Village cannot leave the Katana with a player who is about to be exposed. Check who will hold it and what happens if the holder dies at night before passing it.

Do not quote a private message verbatim unless you can justify how you read it. Verbatim quotes of a PM that only two players can see made the Village doubt the Eavesdropper claim and turned attention onto the recipient.

Katana kills on the claimed Lookout and Census Taker removed the Village's only cross-checks, and the Village then argued over claims it could not verify. Prioritise the investigators whose results corroborate each other and whose claims the Village is relying on.

Agreeing to skip a night attack on Night 1 cost tempo with no information gained. With only three Yakuza against seven Village, early no-action nights hand the Village more time to build a consistent visit list.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza team's unanimous Guilty votes on Grace (a Jester) were followed by Ivan's death to the Jester's revenge, which passed the Katana to Judy and cost the team a holder.

lessons.tip: A Jester's hanging gives the Jester the win and triggers a random Guilty voter's Divine revenge. Don't all vote Guilty on a probable Jester. Vote Innocent when the Guilty majority is already secure, so teammates aren't exposed to revenge. Ivan died this way on Day 2 night, and that moved the Katana.

Never quote a private message word-for-word in public unless you can explain how you could have read it. Erin quoted Heidi's PM to Carol, and the other players asked how she could know. That pressure turned the table on her, so keep reader claims vague and don't quote contents.

Census trios that share one name across nights isolate the odd non-Good player. Killing a claimed Census Taker before the next trio is public stops the village from cross-checking them. Bob's Night 4 kill was correct, but it came late, so kill claimed investigators as soon as their cross-night pattern becomes clear.

A Clerk token held to the end is wasted. Plan to use it on a Day when the village nominee is a Good player you can't save, so the rig removes that nominee without a trial, and teammates vote Innocent so the rig stays hidden. Judy kept the token all game and never used it.

Keep Katana votes identical every night and avoid daytime PMs between teammates. Public PM counts are visible to all, so a teammate PM on Day 5 gave Frank a bloc pattern to cite. Settle everything in the night chat.

tips_feedback.tip: No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them.
tips_feedback.why: The rule is sound, but Erin still sent Judy a Day 5 PM and the public PM count showed it. Frank then cited Judy's PMs as a bloc signal.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night.
tips_feedback.why: Identical Katana votes every night gave no visible split, and the Katana killed Dave, Alice and Bob without the village finding any disagreement among us.

summary: The Yakuza (Erin the Wiretap, Ivan the Ritualist, Judy the Clerk) won alongside Grace the Jester. Grace fake-claimed Sheriff with 'Dave Evil'. Alice's Lookout list showed Grace never visited Dave, so all 10 players voted Guilty. Nobody, Yakuza included, stopped to ask whether a fake claimant that easy to catch was a Jester. Grace won, and her revenge happened to hit Ivan, a Yakuza. The Katana then killed the investigators in order: Dave the Tracker, Alice the Lookout and Bob the Census Taker. Heidi, an Arsonist fake-claiming Medic, was rightly hanged on Day 3 after dousing two players and never igniting. Erin badly exposed herself by quoting Heidi's private message word for word. She survived by claiming Eavesdropper. The village never noticed that Carol's Night 3 profile listed Wiretap and Clerk as decoy roles, and those decoys are drawn from roles held by living players. Bob's Night 3 census (Carol/Frank/Judy: 2 of 3 Good) pointed at Judy, who claimed nothing all game. Even so, on Day 4 Frank argued publicly that Carol was a real Profiler, then cast the deciding third Guilty vote (3-2). The real Profiler died, and with her went the village's last chance. Bob's Night 4 census (Erin/Frank/Judy: 2 Evil) died with him. Day 5 was a 2-vs-1 formality.

lessons.tip: When a claimant is caught in an obvious lie, such as a Sheriff 'Evil' result with no visit on record, consider the Jester before hanging. A lie that easy to catch is the Jester's best play. If you hang anyway, aim for a bare majority, and Yakuza should keep several members on Innocent so the revenge can't hit them.
lessons.evidence: Grace (Jester) claimed Sheriff with 'Dave Evil', did not explain the missing visit, and even invited the nomination. She was hanged 10-0. She won, and her Divine revenge killed Ivan, the Yakuza Ritualist. No speaker ever raised the Jester possibility.

lessons.applies_to: Village (Profiler and everyone reading Profiler results)
lessons.tip: A Profiler's two decoy roles are drawn from the roles of other players who were alive that night, so they usually show which roles are in play. Treat decoys like Wiretap, Clerk or Pharmacist as strong evidence that the role exists, and match them to suspects.
lessons.evidence: Carol's Night 3 profile of Frank showed Clerk, Vanilla, Wiretap. Since Frank was Vanilla, both Clerk and Wiretap were roles of other living players. That nearly proved that Erin, who had just quoted a private message, was the Wiretap rather than an Eavesdropper. Nobody used it, and Carol was hanged.

lessons.tip: Never quote or closely paraphrase a private message you could only have read with a role. If you must use it, steer the discussion without revealing the content, or have a claim ready that fits the timing.
lessons.evidence: Erin quoted Heidi's private message to Carol almost word for word during Heidi's trial. Heidi, Carol, Bob and Frank all flagged it at once, and it became the main lead against her. She survived only because the village didn't cross-check her Eavesdropper claim against Carol's Wiretap decoy.

lessons.tip: Once group results such as census trios narrow the non-Good player to a small set, put pressure on the member who has never claimed a role or night action. Don't hang a claimant whose results check out against known facts.
lessons.evidence: Bob's Night 3 trio (Carol/Frank/Judy: 2 Good) plus Frank's Vanilla claim, which Carol's profile corroborated, left Carol or Judy as the non-Good player. Carol's two profile lists each contained a confirmed true role. Judy claimed nothing all game, yet the village hanged Carol.

lessons.applies_to: Village, especially in the late game
lessons.tip: In a close late-game vote, your vote must match your stated read. Count the votes first: with the Yakuza holding two votes, one Village Guilty decides the trial.
lessons.evidence: In Carol's trial on Day 4, Frank listed reasons why Carol was a real Profiler and pointed at Judy. The trial still ended 3 Guilty to 2 Innocent with Erin and Judy voting Guilty. Bob and Carol voted Innocent, so Frank cast the deciding Guilty, which sealed the Yakuza win.

lessons.tip: Before each night, write your planned target in your will. Then if you die, everyone knows whom you were watching, even though the result itself is lost.
lessons.evidence: Dave tracked Ivan, the Katana holder, on the night he died, and Bob took his census around Erin on the night he died; it came back 2 of 3 Evil (Erin/Frank/Judy). Neither will named the target, so this information never reached the village.

lessons.tip: Kill confirmed investigators in order of threat. Keep a low-profile member unclaimed but always echoing the evidence-based consensus. Avoid daytime private messages between teammates until the endgame.
lessons.evidence: The Katana killed Dave (Tracker), Alice (Lookout) and Bob (Census Taker) in turn. Judy never claimed, voted with the crowd, and survived every day. Erin and Judy sent each other no daytime private messages before Day 5.

lessons.tip: Don't sit on douses. A fake Medic claim falls apart the first time the Katana kills someone you didn't protect, so ignite before you're likely to be put on trial.
lessons.evidence: Heidi doused Dave and Carol and never ignited. After Dave's Katana death exposed her Medic story, she was hanged on Day 3 with no kills.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips).
tips_feedback.why: Every player cited the same concrete contradiction (Grace's missing visit) and hanged her 10-0, but she was the Jester. Without the Jester check from the 'ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged' tip, this tip led straight to a Jester win.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored the Jester part. All three voted Guilty on Grace, and the revenge hit Ivan, costing them a member and their Ritualist. The tip's warning was correct.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current.
tips_feedback.why: Alice posted her Night 1 Lookout list at once, which exposed Grace's fake claim. Bob's and Carol's posted results gave the village a correct narrowing toward Judy and Erin, even though the village misused it.

tips_feedback.tip: No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night.
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Judy sent each other no daytime private messages until the final Day and always voted the agreed Katana target. No private-message link tied them together while Frank's and Heidi's private messages drew suspicion.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you.
tips_feedback.why: When caught quoting a private message, Erin claimed Eavesdropper, a role that had no counterclaimant and that nobody could test. That kept her alive until the Yakuza won.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi waited with two players doused and was hanged on Day 3 without a kill, exactly the outcome the tip warns about.

issues.description: Night 2 moderator summary and record_visits left out Alice's Lookout visit to Bob (Alice→Bob). The night check caught it. Nothing in this game read the visit graph (no Fortune Teller, Cartographer or Scout), so no result was affected, but the omission would have corrupted visit-based results if such roles were present.

During the Day 4 trial vote on Carol, Frank's model call returned an empty answer (finish_reason length, cut off at max_tokens at high effort). The harness had to retry at medium effort. The retry recovered and a vote was recorded, but the token budget at high effort looks too tight for trial-vote prompts.

Players misstated facts a few times. Carol asked Alice who besides Bob had visited her on Night 2, though Alice had watched Bob, not been visited. Bob said Carol had confirmed Erin's PM quote before she had, and his will says Frank was in 'the first two' census trios when Frank was in all three. Frank said Judy had PMed him twice on Day 5; she sent one PM, on Day 4. These are small slips in tracking public information, not rules errors.
